core_obligations: Define the surjection M -> I by e_i -> f_i and check that it is well defined on the module presented by the relations f_i e_j - f_j e_i = 0 (proof lines 24406-24407).
Let K be its kernel and take m = sum a_i e_i in K, so that sum a_i f_i = 0 (proof lines 24407-24408).
Compute f_j m = sum f_j a_i e_i = (sum f_i a_i) e_j = 0 for each j, using the defining relations to reorder the terms (proof line 24409).
Conclude that K is annihilated by I and hence that 0 -> K -> M -> I -> 0 is the required short exact sequence (proof lines 24405-24409).
difficulty_reason: The statement fixes a ring R, a finitely generated ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_n), and the R-module M generated by e_1, ..., e_n subject to the relations f_i e_j - f_j e_i = 0, and asserts the existence of a short exact sequence 0 -> K -> M -> I -> 0 whose kernel K is annihilated by I (source lines 24393-24403). The proof is short and rests on two observations: that the map M -> I given by e_i -> f_i is well defined on the presented module, and that any m = sum a_i e_i in its kernel satisfies f_j m = 0 for every j (proof lines 24405-24409). The second computation is the whole content: it converts the single relation sum a_i f_i = 0 into the statement that each f_j annihilates m, which is exactly the annihilation claim. The author opens by calling the construction 'just a truncation of the Koszul complex' without developing that identification.
